scoring:
z52d rank_O: cluster F by missing theorem, attach reviewer-O re-judgement, score, write clusters.json.
Scoring (explicit): EV = Y * P.
  Y (yield for ES of the strongest statement in the cluster): full ES 1.0; pointwise sub-step a proof would
    need 0.3; structural/thin-family/average/main-term 0.03; none 0.
  P (from reviewer-O plausibility 0..3): 0 -> 0, 1 -> 0.01, 2 -> 0.1, 3 -> 0.4.
    Any statement that is ES-strength (implies ES at large p) gets P = 0.002 if its plausibility is >= 1
    (an ES-strength statement with no handle is not as likely as an open sub-step with no handle).
  Superseded statements (already known in stronger form) have Y = 0 (no marginal yield).
  Ties (EV equal; all ES-strength clusters land at 0.002) are broken by
    h = handle (0 none, 1 formal escape of the named obstruction, 2 specific ingredient that plausibly beats it)
    f = cheap falsifier exists that would kill or promote the cluster (0/1).
  Tier (ii) is ordered by hand: P(provable in a ~1-week lane) x calibration value / cost (EV shown for reference).
  Tiers: (i) could be part of a proof of ES (yield ES or pointwise sub-step);
         (ii) side theorems worth a depth lane (cheap/provable/calibrating);
         (iii) the rest.

clusters.name: Cancellation on the height-tied modular hyperbola (trial/dual/Voronoi/spectral forms)
clusters.statement: For every large prime p: #{(x,y): xy = 4Cp+1, x ≡ y ≡ −1 (mod 4C), C ≥ 1} ≥ 1 (one-sided H⁻ form: ≥ ε·M_BM(p)); first step: any bound |R(p) − M(p)| ≪ p^{2/5−δ}, or a power saving on one dyadic height block, obtained by cancellation rather than the divisor bound.
clusters.frontier: §7.1 (verbatim); PARITY_AUDIT §2–3
clusters.new: Nothing new in substance: Voronoi/van der Corput-per-piece and a trace-formula-over-levels phrasing; Z1855 makes explicit that the pieces ⌈p/m⌉ = q are the pair form.
clusters.obstruction: tied modulus / height-dependent target (PARITY_AUDIT Remark 3.1); B3 for the full form (polylog main term needs near-total cancellation of a p^{1/2}-scale error)
clusters.beats: No member has an ingredient that beats it. The only unexploited structure is the coupling C = (xy−1)/4p itself (formal handle).
clusters.yield: ES for the one-sided form; sub-step (first class-aware single-integer input) for any power saving

clusters.name: Pell / reduction-cycle / E2-primitive roots for the forest or the e-slices
clusters.statement: For every prime p ≡ 1 (24), p > p₀, some element of the principal reduction cycle of ℚ(√p) (convergent P_k/Q_k of √p, ambiguous form), or another explicit non-quasi-polynomial primitive Φ(p) (fundamental unit, binomial/factorial data), is a root whose forest component contains a bichromatic edge (an ES₅ certificate).
clusters.frontier: §7.2 (Astra open question: Pell/class-group cycle data); §3 B1 hatch E2; (J)84 Prop 4.2 kills the coprime CF-norm WINDOW use only; (J)106 kills fixed and least-QNR roots (Dickson)
clusters.new: Z0596: Legendre-type descent that uses primality of p (as for N(ε_p) = −1) — the one item whose proof template is a pointwise theorem at primes. The cycle supplies a power-size (≍ regulator) p-dependent auxiliary set (an M1b-type input B2 otherwise lacks).
clusters.obstruction: B2 (each root is one tied divisor event); (J)84 Prop 4.2 for window uses; the Dickson constructions of (J)106 do not control cycle data (that is the escape)
clusters.beats: Formal only: E2 primitives escape B1 Thm M and the Dickson root constructions; nothing ties the cycle to the class.

clusters.name: Parity / count-congruence / topological index (windmill family)
clusters.statement: For every prime p ≡ 1 (24) a p-dependent finite set S_p with a group action (involution, ℤ/m, S₃) or a mod-2-acyclic complex whose fixed points / critical cells are ES certificates and whose count is ≢ 0 by a formula that sees (·/p) (it must vanish at odd squares).
clusters.frontier: §6 dead end for finite affine involution menus ((J)2 Thm 6.1, CONDITIONAL on H); M5 row of B2_ACROSS_FIELDS; WINDMILL.md (~7000 weights tested)
clusters.new: Z3101: m > 2 group actions (not covered by (J)2); Z3094: class-number parity as the parity source; Z2764/Z2765: acyclicity/Euler-characteristic form (Z2765 notes χ reduces to D⁻ − D⁺, i.e. Theorem K data).
clusters.obstruction: M5/T1 (count must vanish at m², so must see (·/p)); B1-type bar for finite affine menus; genus parity of h(−4p) is congruence data
clusters.beats: Only formally: Rédei 4-/8-rank of Cl(−4p) is not congruence data in p; no member builds S_p from it.

clusters.name: Class forcing beyond parity (full factor multiset, Stickelberger, Lucas primitive divisors, twisted Dedekind reciprocity)
clusters.statement: A property 𝒜 of the joint factorisations of {4Cp+1}_C (or a Lucas/cyclotomic rank-of-apparition structure, or a twisted reciprocity law involving χ(d) of the divisor itself), provable for all large p, that forces −1 into some D_C.
clusters.frontier: §7.6 (full-factor-multiset realisation), §7.7 (general-m Stickelberger); §6 reciprocity/Rédei forcing → parity only
clusters.new: Z1954: Lucas primitive divisors reduce the class mod n to ±1 with the sign a quadratic character — a genuine class-reduction mechanism, but it needs 4Cp+1 to share a primitive divisor with U_{4C}(P,Q) (restates rank of apparition) and is tautological at C = 1.
clusters.obstruction: CLASS_FORCING Thm 2.1 / TWO_POWER_LADDER (parity, never class); privacy of large primes
clusters.beats: Partially: the Lucas ±1 reduction is the only class-level (not parity-level) forcing seen in the 2,995 rows; it does not reach linear-in-p integers.
clusters.yield: ES (if 𝒜 exists); closing lemmas otherwise

clusters.name: One-coordinate polylog witness window (HC, least level C, Vmin, u_min, a_min)
clusters.statement: ∃A ∀ prime p ≡ 1 (24), p > p₀: some ES certificate has its designated coordinate (forest HC(p), least Type II level over all lines, Vmin, I3 interior endpoint u, least e-slice a_min) ≤ (log p)^A.
clusters.frontier: §7.2 (one-coordinate target HC(p) ≪ (log p)^A); two-endpoint/witness-modulus versions are dead (H4_NOT_POLYLOG; POINTWISE_OMEGA13 Thm 5.1); (★)-only version false at 14 primes
clusters.new: Nothing beyond bookkeeping; Z1600 isolates the regime C ≤ (log p)^{log 2} where τ(4Cp+1) can exceed φ(4C).
clusters.obstruction: Landau-type single-integer lower tail; B2 at each window value; possible extension of H4_NOT_POLYLOG energy construction to one coordinate
clusters.beats: None. Value is as a clean falsification target.

clusters.name: High-multiplicity lift (B3 Remark 2.4 hatch)
clusters.statement: A natural lifted variety/weight with fibres ≫ p^δ over each ES solution of 4/p (e.g. solutions of 4/(pk), k ≤ p^δ, k dividing two denominators) whose weighted count has a power-size main term and power-saving error at each p.
clusters.frontier: B3 "does NOT rule out" (high-multiplicity encodings); not a §7 item
clusters.new: Names the hatch; no candidate lift.
clusters.obstruction: B3 (fibres must be p^δ); Z3125 (lift needs enough free variables); the collapse to a sum of ES(p) indicators

clusters.name: Amplified second moment over a polylog family around p
clusters.statement: Σ_{|n−p|≤H}|R(n) − M(n)|²|A_p(n)|² ≤ ½(M(p)A_p(p))² with an amplifier A_p built from (p/ℓ), ℓ ≤ L, H polylog.
clusters.frontier: §6 fixed-p variance / level-Poisson second moment → critical ((J)103 §3)
clusters.new: Bookkeeping showing H must be polylog.
clusters.obstruction: B6 at polylog scale; amplifier is congruence data (B1); variance at polylog windows is the pointwise problem

clusters.name: Propagation / closure / induction (Graham-type maps, rule Λ, Y–Δ moves, scale induction, composition descent)
clusters.statement: A finite set of maps T_i with T_i(n) < n and rules turning ES certificates at T_i(n) (or at smaller scales/levels) into one at n, valid for every large prime n — used with strong induction.
clusters.frontier: §6 Propagation/global-positivity shapes (PROPAGATION_CLOSURE: rule Λ, integral Y–Δ "remain open"); (J)86 amplification criterion
clusters.new: Z3022 overturned in Task A: B1/Mordell–Schinzel do not cover inductive closure (recursion depth grows with p); the real bars are privacy (affine shifts do not transport divisors) and numerator 8 (8/131).
clusters.obstruction: privacy of large primes (SS8 Lemma 2.3); numerator blindness; T1 if outputs are ET-normalised
clusters.beats: No. Note the Z3016/Z3187 "thin polynomial image" argument is wrong for strong induction from all smaller n; the privacy argument is the valid one (Assessment).

clusters.name: Positivity of an exact algebraic expression (Shintani ζ(0, 𝔞) combinations, interlacing families)
clusters.statement: R(p) (or a positive minorant) = Σ_j w_j ζ(0, 𝔞_j) over narrow ideal classes of real quadratic fields attached to word traces (or a real-rooted interlacing average over windows), with an independent positivity proof at non-squares.
clusters.frontier: §6 exact identities (finite fixed-level excluded; growing-level open, (J)10); §6 spectral/interlacing (displayed mechanisms fail)
clusters.new: Shintani cone decomposition as an exact finite handle (Z2845).
clusters.obstruction: T1 (identity must see (·/p)); positivity of a signed combination = spin event (B2)

clusters.name: Regime split / exceptional-character dichotomy (Linnik three principles, Deuring–Heilbronn, Fourier character witness)
clusters.statement: Finitely many regimes covering all large p (by lnr(p), a pretentious distance, or a shared obstructing character), each with its own pointwise existence theorem; in the Linnik form: obstructed windows are killed by ONE exceptional character, which then repels success elsewhere.
clusters.frontier: Reduces to §7.3 (class beyond the BM layer); regime splits by bounded congruence data are B1
clusters.new: Z3003: an exact Fourier identity giving a quantitative character witness for every obstructed e-slice. Rank_O falsifier (scripts/z52d_rank_O_charobs.py, EVIDENCE): at 9 (★)-zeros vs 27 controls, e ≤ 400, obstructed windows are ≈half poverty-type and the subgroup-type ones are mostly the quadratic (genus/BM) character χ_{−e}; non-quadratic subgroup obstructions show no excess at hard primes. No shared exceptional character beyond the quadratic layer.
clusters.obstruction: B2 in every regime; B1 for congruence-defined splits; poverty (B4) dominates failures (also out_Q11 Z1596: 179/183 rich (★) level failures are poverty-type)
clusters.beats: No. The only shared character is the quadratic one, which is the already-free BM layer.

clusters.name: Thin exponential families by recursion / exponent covering / Diophantine finiteness
clusters.statement: ES for all n_s = 15·2^s+1 (and 4^s+297, 4^s+33, 4^s+273), and I3 for 3^k ± 2, 5·3^k+1: certificates recurrent in s on residue classes of s, or exponent coverings, or Subspace/Bennett finiteness of the failure branch; similarly (12^m−1)/11, (8^m−1)/7 by cyclotomic factorisation.
clusters.frontier: §7.8 (thin families still open), §7.17 (I3 thin families); §4 line 16 (no transfer to primes)
clusters.new: Berlekamp–Massey on PROOF certificates of 3·2^s+1/63·2^s+1 (not minimal ones) to find a recurrent template; Niederreiter folding for CF of a/2^k; BHV/Lucas for families with Lucas-like side numbers.
clusters.obstruction: (J)22 Cor 1.5 / (J)68 Lemma 3.1 (no finite ET covering — parameters must grow with s); u ≡ 7 (8) valuation branch is a 2-adic approximation problem
clusters.beats: Yes for the family (recursion in s escapes the finite-covering no-go); irrelevant to primes ((J)84 Thm A).
clusters.yield: partial (one thin family; no transfer to primes)

clusters.name: Primitive ES (gcd(x,y,z) = 1) as a cleaner ES-strength target
clusters.statement: PROVED (Z0866, elementary; rank_O re-checked numerically: 0 primitive Type I among 439 Type I solutions, p < 400): at p ≡ 1 (4) Type I is never primitive and primitive solutions are exactly p = 4ab − (a+b)/m, gcd(a,b) = 1, m | a+b. Open: every large prime p ≡ 1 (12) is of that form.
clusters.frontier: not in FRONTIER (dual of (★): (★) is m = 1, primitive is k = 1)
clusters.new: The k ↔ m duality between (★) and primitive solutions; explains why all 110 primitive failures ≤ 10⁵ are ≡ 1 (12).
clusters.obstruction: B2 (single-integer lottery with smaller mean)
clusters.yield: side (structure lemma + census); the open statement is ES-strength

clusters.name: Explicit / effective constants (BM-free layer via explicit Burgess, explicit M_BM, effective 3/4, explicit Vaughan)
clusters.statement: Explicit (c, p₁) in M_BM(p) ≥ c(log p)² for p ≥ p₁; explicit t ≤ 4ℓ(p) ≤ T_expl(p) with M_t^lev > 0; effective constants in E(N) ≪ N exp(−c(log N)^{3/4}) (remove the Landau–Page modulus from BV).
clusters.new: Bookkeeping only; prerequisite for any eventual "large p + finite check".
clusters.obstruction: none for the statements (B3/B6 for ES)

clusters.name: Numerator 9: finite covering ⇔ no sterile point (is B1 exactly T1?)
clusters.statement: 9/n = 1/x+1/y+1/z for all n ≥ 20 via finitely many polynomial/congruence identities (exceptions exactly {2,5,11,19}); equivalently numerator 9 has no square-mimicking sterile profinite point.
clusters.frontier: §3 numerator blindness (full T1 only for 4 | M; fails for M = 3,5,6,7,11,19 — 9 not listed)
clusters.new: Calibration of B1: if numerator 9 (no T1) is finitely coverable, B1 is "exactly T1".
clusters.obstruction: a sterile point for m = 9 (unknown)

clusters.name: Local-factor floor at pseudosquare-type primes (main term)
clusters.statement: inf_p F(p) ≥ c > 0 for the RESIDUE_HARDNESS local-density factor, uniformly along p ≡ 1 (mod primorials) and p QR mod all ℓ ≤ (log p)^A; i.e. M_F(p) ≫ log²p everywhere.
clusters.frontier: §2.2 (RESIDUE_HARDNESS; z52c); not §7
clusters.new: Pseudosquares as the native hardest list; first-order factor product → 1 along primorial classes (Z2000 sketch).
clusters.obstruction: B3 (main term only); F is itself a CONJECTURE closed form

clusters.name: Non-CRT exceptional-set input from bilinear structure in (u,B)
clusters.statement: Type II/bilinear asymptotics for primes p = 4uBC − u − B with (u,B) in bilinear boxes giving #{p ≤ X : R(p) = 0} ≪ X^{1−δ}.
clusters.frontier: §7.12 (θ > 3/4 needs non-CRT input)
clusters.new: Bilinear structure at fixed C as candidate non-CRT information.
clusters.obstruction: B6; CRT supply cap if bilinear input reduces to forced classes
clusters.beats: Possibly (the only member addressing the CRT cap).
clusters.yield: partial (power-saving exceptional set; nothing at fixed p)

clusters.name: Almost-all ES on thin prime sets / short intervals
clusters.statement: ES (or (★)) for almost all primes a² + b⁴ (2-D large sieve, Friedlander–Iwaniec count); a (★)-prime in every [x, x + x^{0.525}].
clusters.frontier: §5.1 (extensions of the averaged results)

clusters.statement: A finite-rule recursion along the base-b digits (or CF) of p, run ≍ log p steps, outputs a certificate for every prime; closing lemma: its success set is automatic, so its failure set is automatic and contains no structured square set by Cobham.
